name: heredity_lineage_comparison
description: A reusable agent-based heredity-lineage comparison (Module K). Individuals carry a chemical phenotype inherited at fission into a real lineage tree, with a module-specific mechanism: template Eigen ratchet (Q=fidelity^length), compositional GARD split (length-independent, no template), a template-focused hybrid, or a severed non-heritable control. Emits population mean function, functional fraction, size, lineage depth and realized heritability. Reproduces the Eigen error catastrophe at the agent level AND shows compositional heredity escaping the length catastrophe — heredity need not presume a long high-fidelity template.

module.description: Heredity module: template | compositional | hybrid | non-heritable

herd_proc.doc:
Agent-based heredity lineage: individuals carry a chemical phenotype inherited
at fission with a module-specific mechanism (template Eigen ratchet / compositional
GARD split / template-focused hybrid / severed non-heritable control), dividing into
a real lineage tree. Advances ONE generation per tick and emits the population's
mean function, functional fraction, size, lineage depth and realized heritability
(overwrite sensors). ``lineage_state()`` exposes the tree for the Decision view.

This is a coarse-grained agent-based reproduction (the study's proposed primary
method — SSA/agent heredity with explicit fidelity/cost/competition), not a wrapped
ALife engine, and is labelled as such.

_contract.summary: Agent-based heredity lineage — individuals inherit a chemical phenotype at fission into a real lineage tree; template / compositional / hybrid / non-heritable modules compared on realized heritability + functional persistence.
_contract.description: Simulates individuals that divide into a lineage tree, each carrying a chemical phenotype inherited with a MODULE-SPECIFIC mechanism: a template Eigen ratchet (correct sites stay correct w.p. per_site_fidelity, Q=f^length), a compositional GARD split (multinomial fission of an autocatalytic composition vector — length-independent), a template-focused hybrid, or a severed non-heritable control. Advances one generation per tick; emits population mean function, functional fraction, size, lineage depth and the realized heritability (offspring↔parent φ slope). Reproduces the Eigen error catastrophe at the agent level AND shows compositional heredity escaping the length catastrophe.

inputs.temperature: temperature (K; Arrhenius window on the replication benefit)

outputs.functional_fraction: fraction of the live population above the functional threshold (dimensionless)
outputs.heritability: realized heritability — offspring↔parent φ regression slope (dimensionless)

math: template: daughter correct ~ Binomial(parent_correct, per_site_fidelity); Q = f^length
compositional: daughter counts ~ Multinomial(N, grown/Σgrown); φ = cos(composition, attractor)
assumptions: Coarse-grained agent-based reproduction (the proposed primary method; not a wrapped ALife engine).
Template inheritance ratchets (Eigen, no back-mutation); compositional inheritance drifts by multinomial fission (GARD).
Selection-weighted carrying capacity (global competition / dilution); seeded RNG → reproducible.

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).
